card.name: Chewable and other dosage-form wording
card.fires_on: Mostly the ending "able" in "chewable" when it is used for tablets, and sometimes the word right after a dosage-form noun such as "film". It also fires on a few instruction words in how-to steps.

modes.label: Chewable ending
modes.description: The "able" part of "chewable" before the word tablet in administration instructions.
modes.example: 100 mg The 100 mg chew<<able>> tablet can be divided into equal halves.

modes.label: Dosage-form word
modes.description: A form word such as film following sublingual.
modes.example: sublingual<< film>> should be administered when objective signs of moderate

modes.label: Instruction step words
modes.description: Short words in how-to steps, such as not, through, to, or air.
modes.example: the chain pulls<< through>> the loop at one end. Slip chain

card.plain: It marks the end of "chewable" in tablet instructions, and now and then a small word in step-by-step directions.
